seo.title: Grok Imagine Video 1.5 Generator and Reference Workflow
seo.description: Explore Grok Imagine Video 1.5 for text, image and image-reference video, with current limits, reference prompting, safety guidance and canonical quotes.

overview: Grok Imagine Video 1.5 introduces a new xAI video family to MaxVideoAI. The model supports prompt-only generation, opening-image animation and reference-to-video with one to seven images. xAI owns Grok Imagine; MaxVideoAI distributes the launch endpoints through Fal, and Grok remains Fal-only for this release.

hero.title: Grok Imagine Video 1.5
hero.subtitle: Generate one-to-fifteen-second video from text, an opening image or a named image-reference set, with mode-specific resolution and framing controls.
hero.paragraph: Choose Grok Imagine Video 1.5 when the brief benefits from direct prompt generation, first-frame animation or explicit image references addressed inside the prompt. Reference mode supports 480p or 720p and adds a factual per-image pricing input; text and image modes also offer 1080p. xAI is the owner and Fal distributes this MaxVideoAI launch path.

features.title: New first-class Grok family
features.body: Grok is not presented as a hidden variant of another provider. It receives its own family position, prompting advice, evidence gate and future comparison context while remaining unpublished until the complete launch graph is ready.

features.title: Prompt and first-frame starts
features.body: Text mode controls framing with supported aspect ratios. Image mode animates one opening image and follows that source for framing, so the prompt should concentrate on movement, camera and scene response.

features.title: Named image references
features.body: Reference mode accepts one to seven images and addresses them with ordered image tokens. State which source controls identity, wardrobe, object design or environment instead of asking the model to average every image.

features.title: Mode-aware quoting
features.body: The reference scenario supplies the exact image count to canonical pricing and uses a supported reference resolution. Text and image scenarios remain duration-and-resolution quotes without an invented reference surcharge.

decisionCards.title: Best fit: expressive concept scenes
decisionCards.body: Use Grok for short cinematic ideas, stylized character actions and image-led concepts where a clear prompt or a small identity reference set can guide the result.

decisionCards.title: Not ideal: unsupported reference media
decisionCards.body: Reference mode is image-based in the canonical launch contract. Do not describe source video, source audio or a generic document as a supported Grok reference input.

decisionCards.title: Prompt references by role
decisionCards.body: Use the ordered image tokens in the prompt and say exactly what to preserve from each one. This reduces identity blending and makes the output easier to audit.

referenceWorkflows.title: Text-to-video
referenceWorkflows.body: Describe subject, action, camera, setting and ending in a sequence that fits the selected duration.

referenceWorkflows.title: Image-to-video
referenceWorkflows.body: Preserve the first frame and direct the motion that should emerge from it.

referenceWorkflows.title: Reference-to-video
referenceWorkflows.body: Attach one to seven images, name their roles with ordered tokens, and choose only 480p or 720p.

referenceWorkflows.title: Rights and safety
referenceWorkflows.body: Use permitted sources, obtain likeness consent, avoid deceptive impersonation, and review accidental text or unsafe details.

section.referencesTitle: Make reference roles explicit inside the prompt

tabs.label: Story
tabs.title: Define one visible story change
tabs.description: Give the scene an opening state, an action and a stable ending.
tabs.copy:
Subject:
[Appearance and protected details]

Opening state:
[Place, pose, light and composition]

Action:
[One clear performance or physical change]

Ending:
[Final pose, object state and camera framing]

tabs.label: Camera
tabs.title: Direct camera and atmosphere
tabs.description: Choose movement that supports the action rather than competing with it.
tabs.copy:
Framing:
[Shot size and lens character]

Camera path:
[One pan, track, push, pull or orbit]

Timing:
[When action begins, peaks and settles]

Atmosphere:
[Light, weather, texture and expected sound context]

tabs.label: Images
tabs.title: Address every image reference
tabs.description: Use ordered tokens and one role per source.
tabs.copy:
<IMAGE_0>:
[Identity, face, wardrobe or hero object]

<IMAGE_1>:
[Environment, palette or material detail]

Priority:
[Which source wins if details conflict]

Avoid:
[Blended identities, duplicates, malformed hands, logos, captions and watermarks]

tabNotes.body: A short scene still needs a final beat so the result does not end mid-action.
Image-to-video has no separate aspect-ratio control in the canonical endpoint; frame the source accordingly.
Reference mode supports images only in this launch and the supplied count participates in its quote.

globalPrinciples: Keep the main action physically observable.
Protect identity with explicit traits and reference roles.
Match narrative complexity to a maximum fifteen-second clip.
Use sources with permission and avoid deceptive real-person imitation.
engineWhy: Three distinct modes cover prompt, first-frame and image-reference starts.
Ordered reference tokens let the prompt connect a source to a specific trait.
Mode-specific resolution rules keep reference scenarios inside the contract rather than borrowing unsupported 1080p.

demo.title: Grok reference-led night market
demo.prompt: Use <IMAGE_0> for the chef's face, apron and copper pan; use <IMAGE_1> for the rain-lit night-market palette and lantern design. The chef flips noodles once, steam rises into the warm lantern light, and the camera makes a slow push from medium-wide to medium close. Preserve identity and pan shape. End as the noodles settle, with no signs, captions or logos.
notes: Each image controls a different visual layer.
The action and final settling beat are easy to inspect.

proofItems.title: Reference separation

proofItems.title: Coherent action
